messages:
mikael: Heads-up — last night's slab warmup experiment exposed a window where preemptible tenants caused egress bursts that starved dedicated slices.

samir: saw the alert. which region? logs?

elaine: @samir eu-west1; I pulled the pod logs and the hotspot starts ~00:12 UTC. short-lived but noisy.

mikael: exact pattern: tenant A (preemptible) does a large model init + kvcache populate. during warmup it's sending 2x normal egress bursts for ~30s and proxy queues overflow.

samir: that's the classic warmup vs steady-state mismatch. we throttle preemptible egress but warmup bypassed it? can you paste the routing rule? :thinking: 

mikael: here's what the canary had:
```
policy:
  warmup_window_secs: 45
  egress_shaping: preemptible:rate=100mbps,dedicated:rate=500mbps
  bypass_during_warmup: true
```

elaine: bypass_during_warmup=true was the culprit. it was meant to avoid tail latency for cold-start inference but it lets large kvcache fills hog the pipe.

tj: oh — we added bypass to reduce P99 for tiny containers. forgot to limit kvchunk size. we should clamp by bytes-per-second not just requests.

samir: proposal: keep bypass but with escorting: on warmup, route egress through 'escort' queue with token-bucket of 150mbps and per-tenant buckets so no single tenant can burst entire link.

mikael: +1. also reduce warmup_window to 20s and start background prefetch at low concurrency (1) to avoid spike.

elaine: i sketched a PoC policy, pushing gist now: https://gist.github.com/rw/abcd1234

deploy-bot: deploy started: egress-escort-v1 -> canary eu-west1 (uid: d4f3). 4/12 pods updated.

tj: monitorables to add: egress_queue_depth, per-tenant_burst_size, kvcache-fill-rate. alert if egress_queue_depth > 75th percentile + 3 sigma for 30s.

samir: good. also add a cheap regression test: start 3 preemptible inits concurrently and assert tail latency for dedicated requests < 200ms.

mikael: I'll roll the canary to 50% in 15m. anyone object? :thumbsup:

elaine: no objections. will watch the dashboards and post screenshots.

deploy-bot: canary rolled to 50% (8/12 pods). expected stability window: 30m.

tj: if we still see spikes, next step is to add per-tenant admission control at proxy and fail fast for warmup-heavy tenants (soft-403) instead of letting them spill egress.

samir: ack. thanks all — follow-up in #eng-sre if we need cross-team ops.
